stimulus.text:
In August 1801, thousands of people gathered at Cane Ridge, Kentucky, for a six-day camp meeting led by the Presbyterian minister Barton W. Stone. Preachers from Presbyterian, Methodist, and Baptist churches preached at the same time from different platforms, and people wept, shouted, and fell to the ground as they were called to convert. Estimates put the crowd at 10,000 to 20,000 people, in a state whose whole population was about 220,000.

At the same time, some educated Americans followed deism, the belief that God created the world and then left it to run by natural laws, with no miracles and no revealed scripture.
stimulus.source_note: Cane Ridge account drawn from the Disciples Historical Society, Cane Ridge Revival, and the Revival of 1800; deism defined in standard terms.

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from accounts of the Cane Ridge Revival, August 1801.

primary_sources: Barton W. Stone, account of the Cane Ridge meeting, August 1801

stem: According to the passage, the Cane Ridge meeting drew...

options.text: only the Presbyterian ministers of one Kentucky county.
options.misconception: The passage says preachers of three churches took part, not only local Presbyterians.

options.text: thousands of people to an outdoor meeting lasting six days.
a crowd smaller than the population of Lexington.
options.misconception: Background: Lexington then had under 2,000 people, while the Cane Ridge crowd ran to 10,000 or more.

options.text: only people who already belonged to the Cane Ridge church.
options.misconception: Background: the crowd came from across Kentucky and beyond, not from one church alone.

rationales.B: The passage says thousands gathered for a six-day camp meeting at Cane Ridge.
rationales.A: Preachers from three churches took part, not only local Presbyterians.
rationales.C: Background: the crowd of 10,000 to 20,000 was far larger than Lexington, which then had under 2,000 people.
rationales.D: Background: people came from across the state, not from one church alone.
rationales.general:
1. The passage says thousands of people gathered at Cane Ridge in August 1801.
2. It says the camp meeting lasted six days.
3. The meeting was outdoors, with preachers on different platforms.
4. So it drew thousands of people to an outdoor meeting lasting six days.
Remember: a direct question about the passage is answered by the passage’s own numbers.
